steps.title: "No country gets more than 30%. The first retirement years stay in the bank."
steps.body: Michiko's rule after the farewell party, the bookshop and her father's story. It caps her [[home-bias]] and keeps the money she needs soon out of falls. Her rule, not a recipe: sized by her 7 years to retirement.

steps.prompt: Michiko's rule is "max 30% in one country". Japan falls 50%. What happens to her investments at most?
steps.explanation: 30% × −50% = −15%. The rule doesn't stop the fall. It limits how much one country can take, before the rest of the world moves at all.

steps.prompt: Why does Michiko keep her first retirement years out of the market?
options: So a fall right before or after retiring doesn't force her to sell low
Because bank deposits beat shares in the long run
steps.explanation: Money needed in the next few years has no time to recover. Keeping it apart lets the rest wait out a bad market.

t1.title: "Max 30% in one country. Money for my first years without work stays in the bank."
t1.body: Michiko made a rule. Not too much money in one country, because of [[home-bias]]. And money she needs soon stays safe. This is her rule, not a rule for everyone.

q1.prompt: Michiko's rule: max 30% in one country. Japan goes down 50%. How much does she lose from Japan at most?
q1.explanation: 30% × 50% = 15%. The rule doesn't stop the loss. It makes it smaller.

q2.prompt: Why does Michiko keep money for her first years without work in the bank?
options: So she doesn't have to sell when prices are low
The bank always pays more than shares
q2.explanation: Money you need soon has no time to come back after a fall.
